items.label: f03-pagination
items.back: page defaults to 1 and is at least 1; pageSize defaults to 25 and is clamped to 1..100; skip = (page - 1) * pageSize and take = pageSize.

items.label: f04-date-range
items.back: Both dates must parse (else 400 "Invalid date range provided"), startDate must not be after endDate (400), and the span may not exceed maxRangeDays: 180 by default, but the KPI summary passes 365.

items.label: f01-three-streams
items.front: TrackedEvent vs AuditEvent vs MonitoringMetric: what each is for
items.back: TrackedEvent: product and operations analytics (logins, API errors, exports). AuditEvent: compliance and admin accountability (role changes, export requested). MonitoringMetric: technical health time series (latency, error rate, cache hit rate). They stay separate because they have different readers, retention rules and permissions.

items.label: f02-401-vs-403
items.front: Where does a request get 401 and where 403?
items.back: authMiddleware never rejects: a missing or invalid Bearer token just leaves request.user undefined. requirePermission then answers 401 "Authentication required" when there is no user and 403 "Insufficient permissions" when the role lacks the permission.

300 seconds for both; the TTL is fixed inside the Redis client

Neither is cached, because Redis is only used for the job queue

items.explanation: kpi.service.ts:65 calls cacheService.set(key, result, 300) and monitoring.service.ts:74 calls it with 60. Each caller passes its own TTL, which is why a monitoring summary can be fresher than a KPI summary.

items.prompt: processJob runs to completion twice for the same export job (for example a queue redelivery). What happens to its side effects?

choices.text: Both runs write a CSV_EXPORTED event and an EXPORT_COMPLETED audit row each
The second run throws, because the stored fileName already exists
Only the file is rewritten; events are written once per job id
The second run is skipped, as processJob does not reprocess COMPLETED jobs

choices: Both runs write a CSV_EXPORTED event and an EXPORT_COMPLETED audit row each
The second run throws, because the stored fileName already exists
Only the file is rewritten; events are written once per job id
The second run is skipped, as processJob does not reprocess COMPLETED jobs

items.explanation: processJob only checks that the job exists (line 130); it never looks at its status. Each successful run writes a new timestamped file, a CSV_EXPORTED tracked event and an EXPORT_COMPLETED audit record, which is the idempotency gap the guide names.

items.prompt: POST /api/exports/:id/retry is called on a FAILED export job. What becomes of the original job row?

choices.text: It is reset to PENDING and left there; a new job row does the actual work
It is processed again in place, keeping its id and its audit history
It stays FAILED, and only the new job row moves through the statuses
It is deleted, and the newly created job takes over its original id

choices: It is reset to PENDING and left there; a new job row does the actual work
It is processed again in place, keeping its id and its audit history
It stays FAILED, and only the new job row moves through the statuses
It is deleted, and the newly created job takes over its original id

items.explanation: retry updates the old row to PENDING with cleared fields, then calls this.create, which inserts a NEW ExportJob and processes or queues that one. Nothing touches the old row again, so it sits in PENDING and inflates the queue depth that monitoring counts from ExportJob statuses.

choices.text: 401 "Refresh token is invalid or expired", since the first call revoked it
A second new session, because the token's JWT signature is still valid

A second new session, because the token's JWT signature is still valid

items.explanation: refresh looks up a stored row with revokedAt: null and a future expiresAt. The first call sets revokedAt on that row (lines 141-144) before creating a new session, so the second lookup finds nothing and throws 401.
